title: Can someone finish your flow using only a keyboard?
body: A working mouse path can hide a broken keyboard interaction.
narration: A website can work with a mouse and still fail during keyboard navigation. TabProof helps developers turn a keyboard failure into a reproducible test, then check whether a fix actually works.

title: Give the agent a goal.
body: Find Northstar Studio’s in-transit order. Review delivery on November 6. Close the preview with Escape, without applying changes.
narration: Here is DispatchDesk, our controlled test application. The task is to find Northstar Studio's order in transit, review a proposed delivery date, and close the preview without applying changes.

title: Meta chooses the path.
body: Muse Spark reads screenshots, page semantics and focus. Its action tools are limited to keys and text. No navigation recipe is supplied.
narration: Meta Muse Spark interprets screenshots, page semantics, focus, and action history to choose the next step. We supply the business goal, not a navigation script. The agent's only action tools are keyboard presses and text entry.

title: From a goal to an executed route.
tag: RECORDED META SESSION · EDITED FOR TIME
body: Orders → correct customer and shipment → delivery date → preview
narration: Watch this recorded route from the third pair. The agent passes a similarly named customer, opens the correct order, and selects the requested date. It briefly overshoots a control, then recovers. Eighteen real keyboard actions reach the preview. These are observations from the saved Meta session, not a hand-authored route.

title: Escape leaves the preview open.
body: The dialog remains visible. Focus stays inside it.
narration: Now the first Escape leaves the preview open, with focus still inside it. TabProof records the observed dialog state independently of what the model says. This is the specific keyboard behavior we are measuring.

title: Recovery does not erase the failure.
body: The agent eventually exits and reports completion. The failed first Escape remains in the audit.
narration: The agent eventually finds a way out after more actions and reports completion. That does not erase the earlier Escape failures. TabProof keeps eventual recovery and the measured interaction defect as separate results.

title: One controlled source change.
body: Remove the cancel-event handler that prevents the dialog’s default Escape behavior.
narration: The two demo releases differ by one source change: removing the cancel handler that prevents default dialog dismissal. The generated pages are checked for this exact difference. This is a seeded bug in our own test application.

title: Replay the same discovered route.
body: Three fresh browsers per version. Exact original prefix. One Escape. Check closure and focus restoration.
narration: The independent checker replays the original agent's exact route on both versions, in three fresh browsers each. It checks focus along the way, then tests one Escape. A changed route becomes inconclusive instead of a guessed defect.

title: After: Escape closes and restores focus.
body: A fresh Meta attempt takes 17 actions. The first Escape passes. The original route also passes all three corrected reproductions.
narration: A fresh Meta attempt also reaches the corrected preview. Its first Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener. The independently replayed original route passes too. The model outcome and the keyboard measurements are both retained.

title: Three new pairs. Every result retained.
body: 6 valid Meta sessions · 9/9 independent failures before · 9/9 passes after
narration: We ran three new pairs, six actual Meta sessions, with no API failures. All six reached the target. Every original first Escape failed; every corrected first Escape passed. The eighteen independent reproductions are separate checks, not extra model runs.

title: Evidence a developer can use.
body: Start and stop runs. Inspect actions and screenshots. Compare versions. Download an offline report.
narration: Developers can start and stop runs, inspect actions and screenshots, compare versions, and download an offline evidence report. Instead of manually writing the initial path, they can inspect the path discovered by Meta and reproduce the measured interaction.

title: Goal → Meta exploration → repeatable evidence.
body:
Keyboard-only execution. Reproducible evidence. Verification after a fix.

github.com/Alizhan2/Meta-X
narration: That is TabProof: Meta discovers a path, and independent checks measure the fix. This small controlled study is not an accessibility certification. Our code, raw results, and reproduction steps are public.
